paragraphs: Mosquito • Flea • Tick Control
Professional outdoor treatments built for South Louisiana’s long warm season—targeting the shaded, protected areas where mosquitoes rest and fleas and ticks are most likely to hide.
Built around the pest life cycle

Heat, humidity, rainfall, dense plants, standing water, wildlife, and neighboring properties can continually introduce new mosquitoes, fleas, and ticks. Effective outdoor control is about reducing the population and repeatedly interrupting the cycle—not promising an impossible permanent barrier.
Three pests • different hiding places
A mosquito does not behave like a flea, and a flea does not behave like a tick. We look beyond open turf and focus on the conditions and protected areas each pest prefers.
Adults often rest in cool, shaded foliage during the day while water-holding containers and drainage problems can support new generations nearby.
Outdoor flea pressure often concentrates in shaded, humid areas used by pets or wildlife. Yard treatment works best when pet and indoor sources are addressed too.
Ticks commonly use tall vegetation, leaf litter, landscape edges, and wildlife travel areas. Habitat management is an important partner to treatment.

Outdoor flea and tick service is not a substitute for veterinarian-directed pet prevention or treatment of an active indoor infestation. We can treat the yard component while you coordinate the other sources.
What happens at service
We look for shade, dense foliage, water sources, pet areas, leaf litter, and likely pest activity.
The technician treats appropriate harborage and landscape zones according to product labels.
You receive applicable re-entry guidance and practical notes about conditions that can rebuild pressure.
Recurring visits interrupt the cycle and adapt the treatment as weather and pest pressure change.
Choose the right level of control
Both options have a purpose. The best choice depends on whether you want consistent backyard use or short-term support before a specific gathering.
A planned series of 8–10 treatments through the active season.
Targeted short-term reduction before a party, wedding, cookout, or outdoor gathering.
Make every treatment work harder
Treatment performs best when the yard is not continually recreating ideal pest habitat between visits.
Check buckets, toys, tarps, plant saucers, clogged gutters, wheelbarrows, and other containers after rain.
Trim overgrown vegetation, manage leaf litter, and improve airflow in persistently shaded areas where practical.
Outdoor treatment cannot replace veterinarian-directed prevention for pets or indoor treatment when fleas are already established inside.
Tell your technician about drains, ponds, pet zones, wildlife activity, shady corners, or places where bites are worst.
The Grow Green difference
Grow Green is a South Louisiana company with a real local office, trained field technicians, and an owner whose name and reputation are attached to every service.
Licensed, insured, and applied according to product labels.
Applicable instructions, notes, and a local office when you need help.
Flexible service designed to earn your business through results.
Service built around our long warm season, rainfall, and local conditions.

No. Outdoor pest control is designed to significantly reduce activity in treated areas, not create a permanent insect-free bubble. Weather, neighboring properties, wildlife, vegetation, and new breeding can continually reintroduce pests.
The warm-season plan typically includes 8–10 visits at planned intervals. Exact timing can change with weather, season length, property conditions, and the program quoted for your home.

We apply products according to their labels and provide applicable re-entry instructions after service. Keep people and pets away from treated areas until the stated re-entry condition—often once treated surfaces are dry—has been met.

We inspect for likely breeding sources and may treat appropriate water-holding areas with a labeled larvicide when suitable. Containers that can be emptied should generally be drained, and permanent water features are evaluated individually.

Product labels, drying time, rainfall timing, and treatment conditions determine whether service can proceed. Our team monitors the weather and will provide instructions or reschedule when conditions are not appropriate.

Built around the pest life cycle

South Louisiana pest pressure does not take much of a break.

Heat, humidity, rainfall, dense plants, standing water, wildlife, and neighboring properties can continually introduce new mosquitoes, fleas, and ticks. Effective outdoor control is about reducing the population and repeatedly interrupting the cycle—not promising an impossible permanent barrier.

  • Target shaded resting areas

What “control” means: The goal is a meaningful reduction in outdoor pest activity around treated areas. No professional treatment can guarantee a yard with zero mosquitoes, fleas, ticks, or bites.

Three pests • different hiding places

One outdoor plan, targeted with purpose.

A mosquito does not behave like a flea, and a flea does not behave like a tick. We look beyond open turf and focus on the conditions and protected areas each pest prefers.

Mosquitoes

Adults often rest in cool, shaded foliage during the day while water-holding containers and drainage problems can support new generations nearby.

Focus: foliage, landscape edges, shaded harborage, and breeding-source awareness.

Fleas

Outdoor flea pressure often concentrates in shaded, humid areas used by pets or wildlife. Yard treatment works best when pet and indoor sources are addressed too.

Focus: moist shade, animal resting areas, landscape beds, and coordinated source control.

Ticks

Ticks commonly use tall vegetation, leaf litter, landscape edges, and wildlife travel areas. Habitat management is an important partner to treatment.

Focus: transition zones, dense growth, leaf litter, fence lines, and animal traffic.

Outdoor flea and tick service is not a substitute for veterinarian-directed pet prevention or treatment of an active indoor infestation. We can treat the yard component while you coordinate the other sources.

    Straight answers

    Mosquito, flea & tick FAQs

    Still unsure which option fits your property?

    Talk with our local office
    Will treatment eliminate every mosquito, flea, and tick?

    No. Outdoor pest control is designed to significantly reduce activity in treated areas, not create a permanent insect-free bubble. Weather, neighboring properties, wildlife, vegetation, and new breeding can continually reintroduce pests.

    How many treatments are in the seasonal program?

    The warm-season plan typically includes 8–10 visits at planned intervals. Exact timing can change with weather, season length, property conditions, and the program quoted for your home.

    When can children and pets return outside?

    We apply products according to their labels and provide applicable re-entry instructions after service. Keep people and pets away from treated areas until the stated re-entry condition—often once treated surfaces are dry—has been met.

    Do you treat standing water?

    We inspect for likely breeding sources and may treat appropriate water-holding areas with a labeled larvicide when suitable. Containers that can be emptied should generally be drained, and permanent water features are evaluated individually.

    What happens if rain is expected?

    Product labels, drying time, rainfall timing, and treatment conditions determine whether service can proceed. Our team monitors the weather and will provide instructions or reschedule when conditions are not appropriate.

    Can outdoor treatment solve fleas inside my home or on my pet?

    No. Yard treatment addresses the outdoor component. Active indoor fleas may require an indoor pest professional, while pets should receive veterinarian-recommended flea and tick prevention. Coordinating all sources produces the best result.

    How does a one-time event treatment work?

    Tell us the event date when requesting your estimate. Our office will recommend practical timing based on scheduling, weather, and the property. One-time treatment is intended for temporary pressure reduction and does not replace recurring seasonal service.

    Do I have to be home for service?

    Usually not, provided we can safely access the treatment areas and pets are secured. Please give us any gate instructions and identify locked or inaccessible spaces before the visit.

    What areas do you serve?

    Grow Green serves Greater Baton Rouge and nearby Ascension and Livingston Parish communities, including St. Amant, Prairieville, Gonzales, Geismar, Dutchtown, Sorrento, Denham Springs, Walker, Central, Zachary, and surrounding areas.
